description: We are Reverse Climate Change and we aim to address the interconnected challenges threatening humanity’s long-term survival and the sustainability of civilization. Our goal is to explore how climate restoration, ecosystem protection, among other solutions, can reverse environmental degradation and restore Earth's ecological balance. By doing so, we aim to strengthen food and water security, reduce resource-driven conflicts, and create more sustainable conditions for future space exploration.
summary:
We developed the Earth Digital Twin & 1900 Climate Parity Engine, an interactive, zero-click 3D planetary dashboard that models Earth’s coupled biogeochemical, geophysical, and socioeconomic systems from 1900 to 2100 in native 4K WebGL.

Traditional climate monitoring is fragmented across siloed databases, complex orbital telemetry, and abstract predictive models that decision-makers and the public struggle to interpret. Our platform addresses this challenge by synthesizing multi-constellation satellite radar and optical imagery (NASA Earthdata, ASF Vertex NISAR/SAR, UAVSAR JPL, CSA RCM, Sentinel-5P) with dynamic, georeferenced physics engines and an interactive 200-year timeline scrubber.

By calculating the 1900 Climate Parity Index alongside multi-country cohort filters, users can evaluate how planetary restoration interventions—including direct air capture, basalt mineralization, and photochemical methane oxidation—can mathematically restore pre-industrial atmospheric parity by Year 2078. This tool is essential because it bridges deep Earth observation science and actionable global policy, transforming passive climate anxiety into an empirical, verifiable engineering roadmap.

details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

The application is a browser-based, zero-latency 3D digital twin of Earth that couples satellite remote sensing with predictive biogeochemical physics.

  • 3D Georeferenced Globe Engine: Powered by CesiumJS with WebGL hardware acceleration, the globe displays high-resolution satellite imagery overlaid with international boundaries, geographic coordinates, and cartographic place labels. Navigation supports Google Earth-style three-finger tilt/pitch, two-finger zoom, and mouse drag controls.
    • NASA Earthdata: Pulsing thermal anomaly polygons for active wildfires.
    • ASF Vertex SAR / NISAR: Ground deformation zones highlighting tectonic creep and volcanic swelling.
    • NASA JPL UAVSAR: Coastal subsidence and levee weakness overlays.
    • CSA Radarsat Constellation (RCM): Arctic sea-ice extent vectors and trans-oceanic maritime vessel tracks.
    • Copernicus Sentinel-5P: Animated dispersion plumes for industrial methane super-emitters.
  • Biogeochemical Solution Blueprint: The left pane outlines an eight-step remediation blueprint (Direct Air Capture, basalt carbon mineralization, enhanced rock weathering, tropospheric hydroxyl oxidation, soil methanotrophs, stratospheric N2ON2​O photolysis, suboxic marine reduction, and emergency solar radiation management) showing the progress required to reach 1900 Climate Parity by 2078.
  • Country Cohort & Economic Engine: The right pane features a real-time auto-completing search bar that allows users to select individual nations or groups of countries (e.g., United States, China, European Union, Brazil, India). The engine dynamically isolates their combined share of global emissions, carbon sinks, and GDP, calculating their direct percentage impact on the global Parity Index.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Zero-Click Accessibility: The application begins animating and streaming live layers immediately upon page load without requiring logins, complex setup, or GIS plug-ins.
  • Empirical Multi-Constellation Synthesis: Unifies optical, infrared, polarimetric radar (SAR), and atmospheric gas spectrometers into a single coherent interface, overcoming the cloud-cover limitations of optical satellites via microwave radar backscatter.
  • Action-Oriented Quantification: Rather than stopping at climate disaster reporting, the system calculates exact sequestration quotas (12.5 Gt CO2/yr12.5 Gt CO2​/yr) and chemical oxidation kinetics needed to reverse radiative forcing to 1900 levels.
  • Dual-Language Accessibility: Features both an academic research-grade edition and a simplified plain-language edition (/simple/) ensuring that scientists, policymakers, educators, and elementary students can explore the same underlying data.
  • Responsive High-Definition Design: Employs responsive CSS drawer architecture and native 4K canvas scaling (resolutionScale = window.devicePixelRatio) to guarantee clean legibility on smartphones, tablets, laptops, and ultra-wide wall displays.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Democratizing Earth Observation: Transforming inaccessible petabyte-scale NASA, ESA, and CSA satellite archives into an immediate, intuitive public visual asset.
  • Standardizing Climate Parity Verification: Providing an independent verification tool for carbon dioxide removal (CDR) projects, ensuring carbon credits are backed by permanent geological mineralization rather than short-lived offsets.
  • Informing Sovereign Policy Decisions: Enabling national delegations at climate summits (e.g., COP) to simulate how regional emission cuts or investments in direct air capture directly move the global 2078 Parity needle.
  • Inspiring Global Solution Optimism: Demonstrating through peer-reviewed atmospheric math that returning Earth’s atmosphere to pre-industrial health is an achievable engineering challenge within a single human lifetime.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used?

  • Frontend Languages & Architecture: Standard HTML5, CSS3 (Modern Flexbox, CSS Grid, Media Queries, Drawer Transforms), and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+ Modules, Async/Await, WebGL API bindings).
    • NASA Earthdata: MODIS Terra/Aqua Thermal Anomalies (MOD14A1), Sea Surface Temperature (MOD28), OCO-2/3 XCO2XCO2​​.
    • Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF) Vertex: Sentinel-1 InSAR, ALOS PALSAR, simulated NISAR deformation fields.
    • NASA JPL UAVSAR: L-band polarimetric radar flight lines and interferograms.
    • Canadian Space Agency (CSA): Radarsat Constellation Mission (RCM) sea-ice radar and AIS maritime telemetry.
    • Copernicus Sentinel-5P: TROPOMI Level-2 XCH4XCH4​​ and NO2NO2​ column densities.
  • Hardware Optimization: WebGL GPU acceleration optimized for Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4) and standard discrete GPUs with dynamic hardware pixel-ratio handling.

5. How is the project creative?

  • Unified Temporal-Spatial Continuum: The UI links a smooth 200-year horizontal timeline directly with 3D spherical geometry, allowing users to watch atmospheric chemistry, thermal maps, and economic metrics morph in unison as they scrub back and forth in time.
  • Elimination of "Climate Despair" through Engineering: Rather than ending at apocalyptic projections (RCP 8.5), the digital twin models an achievable engineering turnaround, celebrating the specific milestone year (2078) when pre-industrial atmospheric parity is restored.
  • Dual-Audience Architecture: Recognizing that specialized scientific jargon often alienates the general public, the system maintains two synchronized interfaces—a research edition featuring chemical radical kinetics and an accessible edition using plain phrases like "Air Vacuums" and "Turning Carbon into Solid Stone".
  • Interactive Country Cohort Synthesis: Instead of static per-country dropdowns, users can assemble custom coalitions of nations and instantly see their collective percentage weight on planetary survival metrics.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  1. Mathematical & Scientific Rigor:
    • Calibrated atmospheric baseline parameters directly against NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory Mauna Loa records and Antarctic Law Dome ice core data.
    • Modeled multi-gas lifetimes with appropriate decay curves: CO2CO2​ (millennial), CH4CH4​ (11.8 years perturbation lifetime), and N2ON2​O (114 years).
    • Engineered rendering loops using requestAnimationFrame without blocking the main browser thread.
    • Addressed WebGL geometry edge cases (e.g., ensuring semiMajorAxis >= semiMinorAxis in CesiumJS ellipses) to prevent rendering thread crashes.
    • Raised the standard font scale, set explicit line heights, applied -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased, and avoided low-contrast gray-on-gray colors to ensure clean legibility for all users.
    • Designed responsive slide-up overlay sheets and mobile navigation bars so smartphone users experience the same fluid controls and data depth as desktop users.
    • Positioned Solar Radiation Management (SRM) as a temporary, non-permanent thermal safeguard while prioritizing permanent geologic carbon mineralization (12.5 Gt/yr12.5 Gt/yr) and biological methane oxidation as the true restorative drivers.
